summary: Customer requests an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to follow growth and notice changes earlier. They mention biomass and metabolic signals but have not defined them as separate targets. The broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops. They want help turning this into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements.

unknowns: target species and range: which biomass and metabolic species must be measured, over what concentration range, with what required accuracy
matrix and interferences: fermentation broth composition, yeast concentration, nutrients, metabolites, bubbles, particles, and other optically active species
physical state and optical behaviour: initial and final optical regime (clear, turbid, opaque, absorbing), scattering versus absorption balance, and wavelength dependence
temperature and pressure: fermentation temperature and pressure conditions
installation point and distance: whether measurement is in-line, on-line, at-line, or off-line; probe or flow-cell interface; path length; and distance from spectrometer
cleaning and fouling: cleaning regime, sterilization requirements, and fouling potential of the fermentation broth
required accuracy and response time: required time resolution, accuracy, precision, and control-loop requirements implied by 'notice changes earlier'
reference method: which reference measurements are useful and how they should be obtained
